Issued at 235 PM EDT Sat Oct 3 2026

Through Tonight...A slower start to shower and storm development 
today, with higher coverage of clouds this morning helping to 
limit daytime heating slightly. However, as clouds have cleared a 
bit into this afternoon and an outflow boundary from activity 
earlier near the Treasure Coast has pushed northward, isolated 
showers and storms have started to develop. Increasing coverage of
activity is anticipated over the next several hours, with the 
best chances focused primarily across the interior (40-50%). 
Persistent 10 to 15 mph steering flow will help keep showers and 
storms moving, with less of a concern for flooding through the 
remainder of today. Instability from daytime heating will support
isolated storm development, with occasional lightning strikes and
wind gusts of 45 to 50 mph possible. General storm motion will be
to the north-northwest. Hi-res guidance favors activity 
diminishing into the late evening and overnight hours, with mostly
dry conditions anticipated across the peninsula. Isolated showers
cannot be ruled out across the local Atlantic waters, but there 
is low confidence in this. Overnight temperatures fall into the 
70s, warmest along the coast. A high risk of rip currents 
continues overnight at all east central Florida beaches and will 
likely be extended into tomorrow. Entering the surf is not 
advised.

Sunday-Monday...Mid-level ridging situated across the Florida 
peninsula slowly weakens through Sunday, with a broad trough 
extending southward towards Florida into Monday. At the surface, 
high pressure across the Atlantic gets kicked farther offshore on 
Sunday as a front slowly pushes across the southeastern US, where 
it is then anticipated to push into north Florida on Monday. A 
moist air mass will remain in place across the Florida peninsula 
thanks to both south to southeasterly flow at the surface 
continuing to advect moisture towards the area and the frontal 
boundary pushing moisture out ahead of itself towards Florida. 
While PoPs on Sunday are forecast to remain fairly similar to 
today (30-50%), there is an uptick in chances on Monday (50-70%) 
as the frontal boundary approaches. Rain chances will follow a 
fairly diurnal pattern on Sunday, with the sea breeze assisting in
development as it pushes inland. Monday, the pattern is driven 
more by the frontal boundary, though additional support by the sea
breeze will also help. Given the multiple prior days of rainfall,
minor flooding is expected to be a concern through the remainder
of the weekend and into early next week, especially as model 
guidance indicates the potential for some weaker steering flow. 
Isolated to scattered storm activity will also be possible each 
afternoon, though modest instability could be a limiting factor to
more robust development. Lightning strikes and wind gusts of 45 
to 50 mph will be possible with any activity that does develop. 
While showers and storms are forecast to slowly diminish into the 
overnight hours on Sunday, lingering activity across the peninsula
on Monday cannot be ruled out given the front to the north. 
Scattered shower and even storm development across the local 
Atlantic waters will be possible each night.

Given the moist air mass and the predominant south to southeast 
flow, temperatures are anticipated to remain warm across east 
central Florida, staying near to slightly above normal. Highs 
reach the upper 80s to low 90s each afternoon, combining with the 
humidity to produce peak heat indices of 100F and greater nearly 
areawide. Hydration will be key for those spending extended 
periods of time outdoors. Overnight, temperatures remain near to 
slightly above normal in the low to mid 70s.

Tuesday-Friday...Through the remainder of the upcoming week, an 
unsettled pattern is anticipated to persist across east central 
Florida. The aforementioned broad mid-level trough situated across
the southeastern US is forecast to remain in place, with some 
indication of shortwaves moving along it throughout the week. At 
the surface, the frontal boundary approaching from the north is
forecast to stall across the peninsula, generally meandering 
across central Florida. There are some indications for the 
development of a low along the stationary boundary off the 
northeast Florida coast towards the middle of the week, which 
would have implications on beach and boating conditions. There is
some uncertainty relative to timing of development and strength of
the low. This will continue to be closely monitored and 
confidence in the outcome will increase as model guidance comes 
into better agreement on a solution. Overall, a plume of moisture 
along the boundary will support continued higher coverage of 
showers through next week, with PoPs staying elevated (60-80%).
